title: Exploring the Immunefi Bug Bounty Program for Web3 Security Researchers
content:
In the fast-evolving landscape of decentralized finance, security remains a primary pillar for protecting user funds and protocol integrity. For security researchers and whitehat hackers looking to put their skills to the test, structured bug bounty programs offer a transparent way to uncover vulnerabilities responsibly. One notable program listed within the Web3 security space is managed directly by Immunefi, focusing on its own crowdsourced platform and beta release Vaults System.

This article breaks down the details of the Immunefi bug bounty program, covering what the opportunity entails, potential rewards, eligibility guidelines, participation steps, and important risk considerations based on the available source material.

What the Opportunity Is

The opportunity is an active bug bounty program hosted on Immunefi, Web3’s crowdsourced security platform. The program specifically targets security vulnerabilities within Immunefi's own ecosystem, including its beta release Vaults System and website applications.

The Vaults System introduces two core features designed to increase trust: allowing projects to demonstrate proof-of-assets by depositing funds into ready-to-use payout vaults, and enabling projects to conduct whitehat payments fully on-chain via the Immunefi dashboard. Consequently, the bug bounty scope centers around preventing the unauthorized modification of website information, client data leakage, communication leaks, and the loss of assets held within the vaults.

Why It May Matter

For whitehat hackers and smart contract security specialists, participating in well-defined bug bounties provides an avenue to earn compensation while improving the overall security posture of decentralized infrastructure. Immunefi acts as a prominent hub protecting billions in user funds across numerous projects. Reviewing and securing core infrastructure components like vault systems and web applications contributes directly to minimizing systemic risks in the broader DeFi ecosystem.

Who Appears Eligible

Participation as a security researcher is open broadly, but certain restrictions apply regarding geographic location and compliance:

  • Geographic Restrictions: Individuals residing in countries restricted by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) and United Nations Security Council (UNSC) resolutions are ineligible for rewards.
  • KYC Requirements: KYC verification is required to receive a reward. Immunefi may request a researcher's country of residence prior to releasing payments. For critical submissions, government identification must be provided through an external verification service upon confirmation of a valid bug report.

Step-by-Step Participation Instructions

While the source material does not provide a rigid, numbered tutorial for every click on the dashboard, it outlines the core requirements for a valid submission:

  1. Review the Scope and Rules: Carefully examine the program parameters, including the distinction between Primacy of Impact and Primacy of Rules, as well as designated assets and feasibility limitations.
  2. Conduct Authorized Testing: Perform testing strictly adhering to the program guidelines. All smart contract testing must be performed on local forks of either public testnets or mainnet, avoiding direct testing on mainnet or public testnet deployed code.
  3. Prepare a Proof of Concept (PoC): A Proof of Concept is strictly required for all smart contract bug reports and must comply with Immunefi-wide PoC guidelines. Submissions lacking a required PoC will not receive a reward.
  4. Submit via the Dashboard: File the bug report through the Immunefi dashboard, selecting the appropriate asset placeholder if applying under Primacy of Impact guidelines.

What Participants May Receive

Rewards are denominated in USD and paid out directly by the Immunefi team in USDC on Ethereum. The payout structure scales according to the threat level and impact of the discovered vulnerability:

  • Smart Contract Critical: Maximum reward of $50,000, with a minimum reward of $10,000. The reward calculation typically amounts to 10% of the funds directly affected up to the $50,000 cap.
  • Smart Contract High: Capped at up to 100% of affected funds, with temporary freezing multipliers scaling up to a hard cap of $10,000.
  • Websites and Applications Critical: Maximum reward of $10,000 and minimum of $5,000, specifically for impacts leading to direct fund loss without user action, retrieval of sensitive data/files (such as database passwords or blockchain keys), or execution of arbitrary system commands. Other critical web/app impacts are set at a flat $5,000.
  • Medium and Low Severities: Various flat or ranged rewards apply, such as $5,000 for High Primacy of Impact web/app bugs, $5,000 for Medium smart contract impacts, and $1,000 for Low severity findings.

Important Requirements and Deadlines

Key parameters and limitations govern the submission process:

  • Live Status: The program has been live since December 2, 2020, with updates noted up through September 2026. No specific expiration deadline is stated in the source material.
  • Known Issues and Prior Audits: Bug reports covering previously discovered bugs, well-known Gnosis Safe issues, or unfixed vulnerabilities explicitly highlighted in internal Ourovoros audits of the Vaults System are ineligible for rewards.
  • Prohibited Activities: Mainnet testing of deployed code, pricing oracle testing, third-party smart contract manipulation, phishing, social engineering, denial-of-service attacks, and automated traffic-generating testing are strictly prohibited.

Risks, Scams, and Verification Checks

Engaging in Web3 security research requires strict adherence to ethical boundaries and platform verification standards:

  • Avoid Unauthorized Exploitation: Researchers must never test against mainnet code directly or interact with third-party systems outside the defined scope. Unauthorized attacks outside the bounds of a bug bounty program can carry severe legal and financial risks.
  • Platform Verification: Always ensure you are interacting with official Immunefi domains and dashboards to avoid phishing scams impersonating bug bounty platforms or fake support agents asking for private keys or upfront fees. Immunefi handles submissions and communications strictly through their official platform interface.

A Concise Practical Takeaway

To succeed in the Immunefi bug bounty program, security researchers must combine meticulous smart contract testing on local forks with a fully compliant, reproducible Proof of Concept while strictly respecting geographic and KYC obligations.

For more details, review the official program guidelines and parameters directly at the Immunefi Bug Bounty Page.

title: Alibaba Unveils China’s Most Powerful AI Chip and Plans for 10-Trillion-Parameter Models
content:
On Tuesday, September 22, 2026, Alibaba Group presented a significant statement of strategic ambition at its Apsara Conference in Hangzhou. The company unveiled the Zhenwu V900, identified as China’s most powerful artificial intelligence chip to date, and outlined plans for the development of substantially larger AI models.

Developed by Alibaba’s T-Head semiconductor division, the Zhenwu V900 provides three times the performance of its predecessor, the M890. The chip features 216 GB of memory and 1,200 GB/s inter-chip bandwidth. Alibaba indicates that clusters of this new processor can scale to as many as 500,000 units to facilitate frontier-model training and inference. Mass production and commercial availability are scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.

Concurrently, CEO Eddie Wu disclosed that Alibaba’s Qwen team is already training its next-generation model, Qwen 4. Future iterations, specifically Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5, are projected to attain 5 to 10 trillion parameters. This scale would render them approximately two to four times larger than the current flagship Qwen 3.8 Max, which possesses 2.4 trillion parameters. These expanded models are engineered for more complex, longer-horizon tasks as the company advances its pursuit of artificial superintelligence.

Furthermore, Alibaba established a long-term infrastructure objective: expanding its global Alibaba Cloud data-center capacity beyond 20 gigawatts by 2032.

These dual announcements, combining advanced domestic silicon with aggressive model scaling, highlight Alibaba’s full-stack strategy encompassing chips, models, and cloud infrastructure. These developments occur as Chinese enterprises continue to prioritize greater self-reliance in AI hardware amidst ongoing export restrictions on advanced semiconductors.

Alibaba shares increased following the announcement, reflecting investor confidence in the company’s artificial intelligence roadmap.

title: Meta Patches Zero-Day Flaw in Muse Mac App That Could Turn the AI Agent into a Backdoor
content:
Meta has released an emergency hotfix for its Muse AI assistant on macOS after security researcher Patrick Wardle discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow a local attacker to hijack the AI agent.

Wardle, founder of the Objective-See Foundation, disclosed the vulnerability on September 21, 2026. According to his findings, any application or terminal command running under the same user account could modify an undocumented Muse setting called "endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint".

By changing this setting, an attacker could redirect Muse's voice-dictation traffic away from Meta's servers to an endpoint controlled by the attacker.

That could expose users to several risks. An attacker could potentially capture spoken prompts, inject malicious instructions, and steal Muse authentication tokens. The situation is particularly significant because AI assistants such as Muse may have access to sensitive device capabilities, including files, the microphone, camera, location, calendars, and connected services.

Wardle released proof-of-concept code demonstrating the issue and advised users not to install the application until Meta addressed the vulnerability. He described the flaw as making it possible to turn Muse into what he called an “ultimate backdoor.”

Meta said the vulnerability was a local privilege-escalation issue, meaning it could not simply be exploited remotely over the internet. An attacker would first need the ability to execute code on the target Mac, potentially through existing malware or social engineering.

The company has since released a hotfix addressing the vulnerability and said the practical risk was limited because exploitation required local access to the device.

The discovery comes only weeks after Muse's launch and the release of its Mac application. Meta had promoted the assistant's security architecture, including isolated execution environments and a “Sentinel” system designed to reduce the impact of errors and attacks.

The incident highlights a broader security challenge surrounding increasingly powerful AI agents: the more access an AI assistant has to a user's device and services, the greater the potential impact when that assistant is compromised.

If you use the Muse Mac app, make sure you have installed the latest available update.
